## Design

### 2026-10-24 – Date: October 23, 2026

**2h**

Date: October 23, 2026

In this session, I started by considering which main controller board to use and ended up going with the Xiao ESP32-S3 because it's cheaper, but it also limits how many parts I can connect to it. Knowing that the number of parts is limited, I decided to go for at least one of each part to get experience with new parts when assembling them together. One thing that confused me for a bit was the wiring and labels because I had to get the right labels and make sure I had enough ports on the Xiao to make everything connect. After everything was connected, I had a Xiao microcontroller board, two switches, two LEDs, five touch pads, one potentiometer, and one rotary encoder switch. This concludes the parts layout session, and in the next session, I will be assigning the footprints and starting to design the actual PCB.

### 2026-10-25 – Date: October 24, 2026

**5h**

Date: October 24, 2026

In this session, I assigned the footprints and created a custom footprint for the touchpads. When I designed my touchpad, I underestimated how big the pad should be, so I had to try multiple sizes until I got the right fit. I designed my touchpad in a diamond shape using the chamfer option for the corners at about 40%. Once I imported the touchpads, I moved the parts around until most of the wire lines aligned with the Xiao and connected each part to the Xiao using red lines for the main connections and blue lines for the ground and power connections. When everything was set, I added a border around the components and double-checked to make sure I was within the 100mm by 100mm limit that was suggested by the guide.  Next, I moved to view the 3d model of the parts, and I tried it on one of the switches and it was perfect. I moved on to the fabrication process, where I used the fabrication toolkit to generate the files such as the BOM and Gerber Files. I uploaded the Gerber files onto the PCB design website to get a price. Finally, I started a simple code in VS Code to get the main parts done before building and programming the PCB.
